title: Service Call Escalation Matrix
description: Describes how an inbound service contact is classified and routed. Platform neutral by design: this schema names no vendor, no phone system, and no CRM.

version.description: Version of this spec the document targets, for example 1.0.

organization.description: Human readable name of the operation this matrix belongs to.

timezone.description: IANA timezone identifier, for example America/New_York. Required because every time_context evaluation depends on it, and assuming server time is the most common implementation defect.

business_hours.description: Windows treated as business_hours. Any time outside these windows resolves to after_hours, weekend, or holiday.

rules.description: Evaluated in document order. The first rule whose match block is satisfied wins. Order is significant and intentional: put the most specific rules first.

default_rule.description: Required. Applied when no rule matches. A matrix without a default has an undefined failure mode, which in practice means a dropped call.

id.description: Stable kebab-case identifier. Used in logs and reporting, so it must not change once in production.

priority.description: 1 is the most urgent. Four levels is a deliberate constraint. Operations that define more than four rarely honor the distinction under load.

escalation_ladder.description: Ordered rungs. Each rung is attempted, then the ladder waits wait_seconds before advancing.

match.description: Omitting an axis means the axis is not considered. An empty match object matches everything, which is only appropriate in default_rule.

asset_criticality.description: What breaks downstream if this stays broken. Judged by consequence, not by equipment size.

service_condition.description: intermittent is separated from degraded on purpose: intermittent faults are frequently misrouted as low urgency and are often the earliest warning of a failure that will take out a critical asset.

relationship.description: A new caller must never be routed below a contract customer purely for being new. Contract obligations are a floor on response, not a filter on who gets answered.

acknowledge_within_seconds.description: Time to any acknowledgement the caller can perceive, automated or human. This is the number that determines whether the caller keeps dialing competitors.

human_contact_within_minutes.description: Time to a human who can make a commitment. An automated acknowledgement does not satisfy this.

onsite_target_hours.description: Optional. Include only if it reflects a real contractual or operational commitment. An aspirational number here becomes a broken promise in reporting.

notify.description: A role, not a person. Naming individuals here is the single most common reason an escalation matrix rots within a year.

via.description: Email alone is not an escalation channel for priority 1 or 2. It is included for completeness at lower priorities.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for a response before advancing. Zero means notify and advance immediately, used for parallel broadcast.

fallback.description: What happens when the entire ladder is exhausted. Required on every rule.

action.description: Note that plain voicemail is not an available value. If the ladder is exhausted, the caller must still receive something that confirms a human will follow up.

never.description: Explicit prohibitions. Declaring these makes the anti-pattern reviewable rather than accidental.
